doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Nonet, later partnerships and recent projects
title: Daniel Schnyder and the Metropole 'Saxophone Dreams'
summary: They discuss projects people proposed for him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Rich Perry. That would be a whole other thing. He’s a great player but not in the same way as Mark. [He’s] not into the Tristano thing at all as far as I know. There’s another record that interests me, I haven’t had a chance to hear it but, Daniel Schnyder did some string quartet things.
String sextet actually, of Billie Holiday tunes.
He’s somebody I have a lot of respect for as a writer.
A very good player. Good tenor player as well. How did you feel about that date?

It seems, especially that past thirty years, that people have been coming to you now for projects. For example they have you in mind and they propose you these projects, like the thing with the Metropole that you did with . . . Not only the Personal Voice thing with Bill Holman but you did a whole album called Saxophone Dreams.
Yeah. That was a number of different sessions over some years.
Different arrangers for the band. There’s two of my tunes on that record.
